# Phoenix Code extension developer documentation

> Official guides and API reference for developing Phoenix Code extensions and themes.

These pages cover extending the editor. For using Phoenix Code to build a website, start with the user documentation index.

## Getting started

- [Getting Started](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/getting-started): This guide provides an overview on the documentation structure and how to get started with the Phoenix Code API documentation!
- [Creating Themes](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/creating-themes): This document outlines how to create your own themes for Phoenix Code.
- [Creating Extensions](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/creating-extensions): This document outlines how to write your own extensions for Phoenix Code.
- [Use node.js from your extension](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/creating-node-extensions): This document outlines how to create node extensions for Phoenix Code.
- [Debugging Extensions](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/debugging-extensions): The Debug menu provides several options for extension development.
- [Publishing Themes & Extensions](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/publishing-extensions): This document outlines how to publish your Extensions/Themes to Phoenix Code Extension store.
- [Available Standard Libraries](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/available-standard-libs): The following standard libraries are available inside Phoenix Code:

## How To

- [Show Dialogs](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/How-To/Dialogs): This document outlines the basic features of working with Dialogs, including:
- [Add Menus, Menu items and Keyboard Shortcuts](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/How-To/Menus): This document outlines the basic features of working with Menus, including:
- [How to create Panels](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/How-To/Panels): In Phoenix Code, Panels are of two types :- Plugin Panel and Bottom Panel.
- [Add an indicator icon on the status bar](https://docs.phcode.dev/api/How-To/StatusBar): This document outlines the basic features of working with Status Bar, including:
